items.title: Final Fantasy XIV on Switch 2 is Better Than Anyone Expected
items.summary: Final Fantasy XIV is shaping up to be one of the Switch 2's most technically ambitious ports, with Square Enix targeting stable performance while bringing the full MMORPG experience to Nintendo's latest hybrid console.
items.content:
Final Fantasy XIV is shaping up to be one of the Switch 2's most technically ambitious ports, with Square Enix targeting stable performance while bringing the full MMORPG experience to Nintendo's latest hybrid console.

When Final Fantasy XIV was first announced for Nintendo Switch 2, skepticism was understandable. This is, after all, an MMORPG that has been evolving continuously for more than a decade. It spans multiple expansions, supports hundreds of players in shared social spaces, features massive raids, sprawling cities, and some of the busiest online hubs in gaming.

Translating all of that to a handheld system seemed like an enormous technical challenge. But it's clear that Square Enix seems to be taking on the task very seriously based on our early impressions of the game so far today at launch.

Producer and director Naoki Yoshida (Yoshi-P) has confirmed that the team has prioritized consistent performance over raw frame rate, targeting a stable 30 FPS throughout the majority of gameplay . Rather than chasing higher numbers, the focus has been on maintaining smooth combat and reliable frame pacing during the content players spend most of their time enjoying things like main scenario quests, dungeons, trials, raids, crafting, gathering, and exploration.

"I want to be honest with you: we are working really hard on the optimisation. We are striving to get the best performance. I think with the towns, you may see a lower framerate, only because there are so many players that are rendered on the screen.

The Nintendo Switch 2 is a wonderful console, and I think you can choose the way you want to play. You are more free to choose which mode to play in, so I hope that players will find the way to play that is most suited for themselves."

- Naoki Yoshida (Yoshi-P), game director, during a press conference

Cities like Limsa Lominsa regularly fill with hundreds of player characters showing off mounts, glamour sets, minions, and particle-heavy abilities. Even on significantly more powerful hardware, those areas have historically been among the game's toughest rendering scenarios. Square Enix has been transparent that these locations are where Switch 2 players are most likely to see performance fluctuate, but the team says it has spent considerable time optimizing the experience leading up to launch.

From the time I've spent with the game so far, you can definitely feel the impact. But since these are social gathering areas or just dialogue- and menu-heavy environments, it's not really a big detractor from gameplay. When you're outside of the city doing quests or in an instance, it's been very smooth so far.

I picked up playing with my level 30 Gladiator I abandoned a few years ago on PC, so it's been a little bit of a learning curve so far. Fortunately, if you really want to, you don't have to play in handheld mode or using a controller since there's mouse support on Switch 2, including both USB options and the Joy-Con's mouse mode.

"As everyone already knows, the Nintendo Switch 2 is an amazing piece of hardware. If you place it in the dock, you can play in TV mode. If you use it in Portable mode, you can carry it and play it at your leisure. For example, when challenging a high-difficulty Raid, you can play on TV while connecting a mouse and keyboard, and then you can craft and gather while in Portable mode. I feel like this will enable a play style that is unique to Nintendo Switch 2.

Following the announcement at the keynote speech, I also saw some voices on social media asking, 'Is it going to be alright spec-wise?', but we are thoroughly optimizing it. There are no performance issues at all during actual content. It's much more hectic when you're in a town with a lot of characters, though I think it should run stably around 30 frames there as well. The performance is better in the actual content, so I think it should be okay, and you should not worry."

- Naoki Yoshida (Yoshi-P), game director, in an interview with Famitsu reported by RPGSite

Unlike many MMORPG adaptations, this isn't a separate handheld version with isolated servers or reduced functionality. Switch 2 players log into the same persistent world as everyone else across PC, PlayStation, and Xbox. Every expansion, every raid, every social space, every seasonal event, and every update arrives together, allowing players to seamlessly continue their existing characters wherever they choose to play in both handheld and docked modes.

items.title: Final Fantasy XIV is finally available on Switch 2, Complete Edition 30% off for next few days
items.summary: After announcing it earlier this year, Square Enix has finally released Final Fantasy XIV on the Nintendo Switch 2. Available in its “Free Trial,” “Starter
items.content:
After announcing it earlier this year , Square Enix has finally released Final Fantasy XIV on the Nintendo Switch 2. Available in its “Free Trial,” “Starter Edition,” and “Complete Edition” formats, players can now journey across the land of Hydaelyn from the comfort of their hybrid console. Playing an MMO from the toilet does sound like an interesting way to pass the time while doing your business, in-game and out.

To commemorate the occasion, the “Complete Edition” is currently 30% off on the eShop for the next few days. Including 30 days of game access as well as every expansion (of which there are six), you can grab it for $41.99 until August 8th, 2026. The “Starter Edition,” meanwhile, will run you $20 and includes the base game with its four expansions and 30 days of game access. The “Free Trial,” meanwhile, is probably the better option for people unfamiliar with MMOs.

Unlike other trials for MMOs, Final Fantasy XIV’s Free Trial is actually ludicrously generous. Granting access to the full campaign and its first three expansions, the only real restrictions involve interacting with other players. You cannot use the Party Finder, cannot chat, can’t register friends, cannot trade, and cannot buy houses. You’re also capped to level 80 and only able to access 18 of the 22 available jobs, though you can still experience the main story of Final Fantasy XIV. Think of it more like an extended demo rather than a sampler.

The game will take up a whopping 117 GB on your Switch 2, but if you’re a Final Fantasy faithful, then that’s probably worth it. I might give the trial a shot since playing something like an MMO on a portable device is still pretty novel.

items.title: Final Fantasy 14 Switch 2 Launch Is a Surprise Success With One Huge Catch
Final Fantasy XIV Out Now on Switch 2, Complete Edition 30% Off Until August 8
items.summary: Square Enix has officially launched Final Fantasy XIV for the Nintendo Switch 2 today. To celebrate the release of [...]
items.content:
Square Enix has officially launched Final Fantasy XIV for the Nintendo Switch 2 today.

To celebrate the release of the game, the Complete Edition is currently available for $41.99, which is a 30 percent discount on the Nintendo eShop until August 8. After this the price will increase to $59.99.

The Switch 2 version will not require a Nintendo Switch Online subscription, however, a separate monthly subscription from the other versions will be required. Users who subscribe on other platforms will receive a 50 percent discount on the subscription for the Switch 2 version.

The Free Trial version of the game lets gamers play through the base game and the first three story expansions Heavensward , Stormblood , and Shadowbringers for free. The rest of the content requires a subscription

The Evercold expansion will launch in January 2027 for all platforms.

items.title: Final Fantasy XIV launches for Switch 2 today
items.content:
0 Square Enix is bringing Final Fantasy XIV to Switch 2 today! The game will require a subscription fee (as it does on other platforms), but Switch Online won’t be necessary to play. You can see all the details below, and please note that you’ll need 117GB to downoad this one.

To celebrate the game’s release on Nintendo Switch 2, both versions of the Complete Edition are 30% off until Thursday, 13 August 2026!

To help ensure a stable launch experience, subscription fees will be waived for approximately one month following release.

Following this period, the 30-day free play period included when registering a new platform will begin. Once this time has elapsed, a subscription fee will be required to continue playing. A separate subscription is required to play the Nintendo Switch 2 version, regardless of whether you are subscribed on another platform. However, if you have remaining game time on other platforms, the Nintendo Switch 2 subscription will be available at half price.

(Please note that the half price discount is not available while free game time is active on other platforms.)

A subscription to Nintendo Switch Online is not required to play FINAL FANTASY XIV.

A Square Enix account and Nintendo account are required to play FINAL FANTASY XIV.

Upon launching for the very first time, the Nintendo Switch 2 user profile will be linked to your Square Enix account. You will not be able to unlink the accounts or transfer to another account once linked. Please be careful and confirm that both accounts are correct before linking.

If you are currently playing on another platform, such as the Windows version, and would like to continue playing with the same character on the Nintendo Switch 2 version, you must select the service account that you have already been using to play when prompted to register a license. After this, follow the additional instructions displayed on screen. Please note that you will be unable to play as your existing character if you select the option to create a new service account.

When creating a new character, you will be prompted to select a starting World. Special bonuses are offered for creating a character on certain Worlds.

Learn more about bonuses earned for creating characters on New and Preferred Worlds. Visit the Server Status page for a list of Worlds that are currently classified as New or Preferred.

Depending on the circumstances, there may be times when no Worlds are classified as New or Preferred, or character creation is temporarily unavailable on certain Worlds.

Payment for subscription fees, additional services, and optional items will require FFXIV Coins, which can be purchased from the Nintendo eShop.

Once purchased, FFXIV Coins can be used on the FINAL FANTASY XIV: Mog Station for subscription fees and other account services, or on the FINAL FANTASY XIV Online Store for optional items.

items.title: The Second Job For FF14's Evercold Expansion May Have Already Been Teased
You can try the newly-launched Switch 2 port of Final Fantasy 14 for free, right now, if you have a spare 117GB
items.summary: "To help ensure a stable launch experience, subscription fees will be waived for approximately one month following release," says Square Enix.
items.content:
Image credit: Eurogamer / Square Enix / Nintendo News by Dom Peppiatt Deputy Editorial Director Published on Aug. 4, 2026, 1:46 p.m. 8 comments Follow Final Fantasy XIV: A Realm Reborn - Collector's Edition Have you heard of the critically acclaimed MMORPG Final Fantasy 14 ? Well, today the oft-memed Final Fantasy online title has arrived on Switch 2 , marking a very quick turnaround between the announcement of the port at the end of June and its actual release date.

Perhaps the best news is that the game arrives on Nintendo's hybrid console with a free trial, which includes quite a bit of content: the base game and three pretty sizeable expansions in Heavensward , Stormblood and Shadowbringers . You can download this now, and play today, at absolutely no cost. You will, however, have to set up both a Nintendo Switch Online account and a Square Enix account in order to access the game, though a subscription to Nintendo Switch Online is not required to play. You will be capped at level 80 in the free trial, and you don't get to use the full suite of multiplayer features, engage in PvP, or try out the Ultimate Raids. Still, as a way of seeing if this critically- and commercially-successful MMORPG is for you, it's a very good way in.

And it gets better. "To help ensure a stable launch experience, subscription fees will be waived for approximately one month following release," noted Square Enix. "Following this period, the 30-day free play period included when registering a new platform will begin. Once this time has elapsed, a subscription fee will be required to continue playing. A separate subscription is required to play the Nintendo Switch 2 version, regardless of whether you are subscribed on another platform."

However, if you immediately purchase any of the Final Fantasy 14 Switch 2 editions available to pre-order, you will not be able to take advantage of the free trial.. It's very much a 'try before you buy' sort-of deal. If it helps make your decision, Square Enix has announced that both versions of the Complete Edition are 30 percent off until Thursday, 13th August, 2026. This means FF14 on Switch 2 is currently $41.99/£31.49 instead of the usual $59.99 / £44.99.

Additionally, if you have an active subscription on another platform (say, PS5 or PC), you will be able to play on Switch 2 for a discounted 50 percent off. You'll still be paying twice, but that may take some of the sting out of the issue.

There's one small but also large downside, though: the free trial weighs in at a massive 117.2GB - a file size larger than even FF7 Rebirth and Remake, both of which were 90GB. I hope you have some bonus storage in your Switch 2, because even if you're not carrying much else around on the console's internal 256GB, this is going to take up a lot of your digital real estate.

items.title: Final Fantasy 14 launches on Switch 2 today, Complete Edition is 30% off for a limited time
items.summary: Square Enix’s MMORPG comes to Nintendo for the first time…
items.content:
Square Enix’s MMORPG comes to Nintendo for the first time

Video Game News 4th Aug 2026 / 1:06 pm Posted by Chris Scullion Final Fantasy 14 launches on Nintendo Switch 2 today.

Following a poor 2010 release, Square Enix ‘s MMORPG was reworked and relaunched on PS3 and PC in 2013 as Final Fantasy 14: A Realm Reborn, where it was received far better by fans.

The game continues to enjoy a large following in the 13 years that have followed, and has been released on a number of formats over the years, including PS4 in 2014, PS5 in 2021 and Xbox Series X/S in 2024.

Now it’s Switch 2 ‘s turn to get Final Fantasy 14, with Square Enix bringing the game to Nintendo players for the first time.

As with other formats, Final Fantasy 14 includes a lengthy Free Trial version – which is around 117 GB in size – as well as Starter Edition and Complete Edition versions.

To celebrate the game’s launch on Switch 2, the Complete Edition is 30% off on the Switch 2 eShop until August 8, meaning it’s currently $41.99 / £31.49 instead of its normal price of $59.99 / £44.99.

Players who purchase the Starter or Complete Editions will get 30 days of play for free, after which they will have to pay a monthly subscription to continue playing with their full benefits. If they stop paying their subscription, their character’s progress will freeze and players won’t be able to drop down to the Free Trial version.

Newcomers, then, may wish to start with the Free Trial, which lets them play through the entirety of the base game A Realm Reborn as well as its first three story expansions – Heavensward, Stormblood and Shadowbringers – entirely free with no subscription cost.

The Free Trial does have restrictions, which mainly involve interacting with other players. This includes Party Finder, Chat, Chat Groups, registering friends, Free Companies, trading, the Market Board and the Moogle Delivery service.

Players are capped at level 80 (instead of level 100) and have access to 18 playable jobs instead of 22. They also can’t take part in Ultimate Raids, PvP content or housing features.

Other than the above, however, the game and its first three expansions are fully playable with the Free Trial, meaning players who simply wish to play through the story should be able to do so free of charge.

Just days before its release, the Nintendo Switch 2 version of Final Fantasy 14 has received a lengthy look with first gameplay.

Square Enix hosted a live stream for the MMORPG earlier today. It was a lengthy one focusing on the Nintendo Switch 2 version, and we’ve got about two hours of footage here.

Note that Final Fantasy 14 has touchscreen support on Nintendo Switch 2. As previously mentioned, you’ll also be able to use a mouse and keyboard .

Here’s some information about Final Fantasy 14:

For newcomers, the Free Trial includes four award-winning titles

Join over 30 million adventurers worldwide and take part in an epic and ever-changing Final Fantasy. Experience all the hallmarks of the best-selling franchise – an unforgettable story, exhilarating battles, and a myriad of diverse and captivating environments to explore.

Party up with friends or play solo! Experience all the main story dungeons on your own by calling upon NPC allies to fight by your side.

Get a look at the gameplay for Final Fantasy 14 on Nintendo Switch 2 below.

Final Fantasy 14 hits Nintendo’s latest console on August 4, 2026. For those that missed it, Square Enix just recently shared a truckload of information about what’s planned for the game – catch up on it all here .
